annotations.title: Estimate Social Security benefit by claiming age

description: Computes Social Security claiming-age figures from the person's birth month and year and their estimated benefit at full retirement age. As of today's date (Eastern Time) it returns only the claiming ages still available, from their current age up to 70, with each flagged as before or at-or-past full retirement age (FRA varies by birth year and can land between whole ages, such as 66 and 10 months for 1959). Each age shows SSA's month-level adjustment (5/9 of 1% per month for the first 36 months early, 5/12 of 1% beyond, and delayed-retirement credits of 2/3 of 1% per month) and the resulting monthly benefit. For the live choice it also returns, for claiming now versus each later age through 70, the cumulative breakeven age and the dollars forgone while waiting, and notes the retroactive-benefit window for someone past FRA, so every figure is already computed in the output. Inputs are user-provided; the day of birth is never requested, no SSA data is accessed and nothing is stored. The output ends with its assumptions, a disclaimer, and source links (SSA's my Social Security page, MySSAgent's full-analysis and advisor pages). Directional estimate, not advice.

birth_month.description: The month the person was born, 1 (January) to 12 (December). Month and year only; the day of birth is not needed.

birth_year.description: The year the person was born (e.g. 1962).

fra_monthly_benefit.description: Their estimated monthly benefit at full retirement age, in dollars — shown on their SSA statement at ssa.gov/myaccount. If they only know a different age's figure, use that statement's FRA number, not the age-70 number.

married.description: Optional. Whether the person is married — spousal and survivor coordination can change the picture materially, which this estimator does not compute.
